No-arbitrage principle (p.87)
The no-arbitrage principle says there is no arbitrage strategy $\Phi$.
That is, there is no strategy $\Phi$ such that
V_0(\Phi) = 0, \quad V_n(\Phi) \ge 0 \quad \text{and} \quad P(V_n(\Phi) > 0) > 0
Let's read the three parts.
I start with nothing.
I can never end up below zero.
And there is some chance I end up above zero.
That's free money with no risk.

I put that money in the bond.
Now my starting value is $0$, and my final value is even bigger.
